L16: ## 29.43 Valuative criteria
L17: 
L18: We have already discussed the valuative criterion for universal closedness and for separatedness in Schemes, Sections 【11†26.20】 and 【12†26.22】. In this section we will discuss some consequences and variants. In Limits, Section 【13†32.15】 we will show that it suffices to consider discrete valuation rings when working with locally Noetherian schemes and morphisms of finite type.
L19: 
L20: reference
L21: 【14†Lemma 29.43.1 (Valuative criterion for properness).】 Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$. Assume $f$ is of finite type and quasi-separated. Then the following are equivalent
L22: 
L23:   1. $f$ is proper,
L24: 
L25:   2. $f$ satisfies the valuative criterion (Schemes, Definition 【15†26.20.3】),
L26: 
L27:   3. given any commutative solid diagram
L28: 
L29: \[ \xymatrix{ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K) \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d] \\ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A) \ar[r] \ar@{-->}[ru] & Y } \]
L30: where $A$ is a valuation ring with field of fractions $K$, there exists a unique dotted arrow making the diagram commute.
L31: 
L32: Proof. Part (3) is a reformulation of (2). Thus the lemma is a formal consequence of Schemes, Proposition 【16†26.20.6】 and Lemma 【17†26.22.1】, Lemma 【18†26.22.2】, and the definitions. $\square$
L33: 
L34: One usually does not have to consider all possible diagrams when testing the valuative criterion. We will call a valuative criterion as in the next lemma a “refined valuative criterion”.
L35: 【19†Lemma 29.43.2.】 Let $f : X \to S$ and $h : U \to X$ be morphisms of schemes. Assume that $f$ and $h$ are quasi-compact and that $h(U)$ is dense in $X$. If given any commutative solid diagram
L36: 
L37: \[ \xymatrix{ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K) \ar[r] \ar[d] & U \ar[r]^ h & X \ar[d]^ f \\ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A) \ar[rr] \ar@{-->}[rru] & & S } \]
L38: where $A$ is a valuation ring with field of fractions $K$, there exists a unique dotted arrow making the diagram commute, then $f$ is universally closed. If moreover $f$ is quasi-separated, then $f$ is separated.
L39: 
L40: Proof. To prove $f$ is universally closed we will verify the existence part of the valuative criterion for $f$ which suffices by Schemes, Proposition 【16†26.20.6】. To do this, consider a commutative diagram
L41: \[ \xymatrix{ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K) \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d] \\ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A) \ar[r] & S } \]
L42: where $A$ is a valuation ring and $K$ is the fraction field of $A$. Note that since valuation rings and fields are reduced, we may replace $U$, $X$, and $S$ by their respective reductions by Schemes, Lemma 【20†26.12.7】. In this case the assumption that $h(U)$ is dense means that the scheme theoretic image of $h : U \to X$ is $X$, see Lemma 【21†29.6.7】. We may also replace $S$ by an affine open through which the morphism $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A) \to S$ factors.
L43: Thus we may assume that $S = \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(R)$.
L44: Let $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(B) \subset X$ be an affine open through which the morphism $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K) \to X$ factors. Choose a polynomial algebra $P$ over $B$ and a $B$-algebra surjection $P \to K$. Then $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(P) \to X$ is flat. Hence the scheme theoretic image of the morphism $U \times _ X \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(P) \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(P)$ is $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(P)$ by Lemma 【22†29.26.16】. By Lemma 【23†29.6.5】 we can find a commutative diagram
L45: \[ \xymatrix{ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K') \ar[r] \ar[d] & U \times _ X \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(P) \ar[d] \\ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A') \ar[r] & \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(P) } \]
L46: where $A'$ is a valuation ring and $K'$ is the fraction field of $A'$ such that the closed point of $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A')$ maps to $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K) \subset \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(P)$. In other words, there is a $B$-algebra map $\varphi : K \to A'/\mathfrak m_{A'}$. Choose a valuation ring $A'' \subset A'/\mathfrak m_{A'}$ dominating $\varphi (A)$ with field of fractions $K'' = A'/\mathfrak m_{A'}$ (Algebra, Lemma 【24†10.50.2】). We set
L47: \[ C = \{ \lambda \in A' \mid \lambda \bmod \mathfrak m_{A'} \in A''\} . \]
L48: 
L49: which is a valuation ring by Algebra, Lemma 【25†10.50.10】. As $C$ is an $R$-algebra with fraction field $K'$, we obtain a commutative diagram
L50: 
L51: \[ \xymatrix{ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K') \ar[r] \ar[d] & U \ar[r] & X \ar[d] \\ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(C) \ar[rr] \ar@{-->}[rru] & & S } \]
L52: as in the statement of the lemma. Thus a dotted arrow fitting into the diagram as indicated. By the uniqueness assumption of the lemma the composition $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A') \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(C) \to X$ agrees with the given morphism $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A') \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(P) \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(B) \subset X$.
L53: Hence the restriction of the morphism to the spectrum of $C/\mathfrak m_{A'} = A''$ induces the given morphism $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K'') = \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A'/\mathfrak m_{A'}) \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K) \to X$. Let $x \in X$ be the image of the closed point of $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A'') \to X$. The image of the induced ring map $\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to A''$ is a local subring which is contained in $K \subset K''$.
L54: Since $A$ is maximal for the relation of domination in $K$ and since $A \subset A''$, we have $A = K \cap A''$. We conclude that $\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to A''$ factors through $A \subset A''$. In this way we obtain our desired arrow $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A) \to X$.
L55: Finally, assume $f$ is quasi-separated. Then $\Delta : X \to X \times _ S X$ is quasi-compact. Given a solid diagram
L56: 
L57: \[ \xymatrix{ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K) \ar[r] \ar[d] & U \ar[r]^ h & X \ar[d]^\Delta \\ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A) \ar[rr] \ar@{-->}[rru] & & X \times _ S X } \]
L58: where $A$ is a valuation ring with field of fractions $K$, there exists a unique dotted arrow making the diagram commute. Namely, the lower horizontal arrow is the same thing as a pair of morphisms $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A) \to X$ which can serve as the dotted arrow in the diagram of the lemma. Thus the required uniqueness shows that the lower horizontal arrow factors through $\Delta $.
L59: Hence we can apply the result we just proved to $\Delta : X \to X \times _ S X$ and $h : U \to X$ and conclude that $\Delta $ is universally closed. Clearly this means that $f$ is separated. $\square$
L60: 【26†Remark 29.43.3.】 The assumption on uniqueness of the dotted arrows in Lemma 【19†29.43.2】 is necessary (details omitted). Of course, uniqueness is guaranteed if $f$ is separated (Schemes, Lemma 【17†26.22.1】).
L61: 
L62: 【27†Lemma 29.43.4.】 Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $S$. Let $s \in S$ and $x \in X$, $y \in Y$ points over $s$.
L63:   1. Let $f, g : X \to Y$ be morphisms over $S$ such that $f(x) = g(x) = y$ and $f^\sharp _ x = g^\sharp _ x : \mathcal{O}_{Y, y} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$. Then there is an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ with $f|_ U = g|_ U$ in the following cases
L64: 
L65:     1. $Y$ is locally of finite type over $S$,
L66: 
L67:     2. $X$ is integral,
L68: 
L69:     3. $X$ is locally Noetherian, or
L70: 
L71:     4. $X$ is reduced with finitely many irreducible components.
L72:   2. Let $\varphi : \mathcal{O}_{Y, y} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ be a local $\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$-algebra map. Then there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$ and a morphism $f : U \to Y$ mapping $x$ to $y$ with $f^\sharp _ x = \varphi $ in the following cases
L73: 
L74:     1. $Y$ is locally of finite presentation over $S$,
L75: 
L76:     2. $Y$ is locally of finite type and $X$ is integral,
L77: 
L78:     3. $Y$ is locally of finite type and $X$ is locally Noetherian, or
L79:     4. $Y$ is locally of finite type and $X$ is reduced with finitely many irreducible components.
L80: 
L81: Proof. Proof of (1). We may replace $X$, $Y$, $S$ by suitable affine open neighbourhoods of $x$, $y$, $s$ and reduce to the following algebra problem: given a ring $R$, two $R$-algebra maps $\varphi , \psi : B \to A$ such that
L82: 
L83:   1. $R \to B$ is of finite type, or $A$ is a domain, or $A$ is Noetherian, or $A$ is reduced and has finitely many minimal primes,
L84:   2. the two maps $B \to A_\mathfrak p$ are the same for some prime $\mathfrak p \subset A$,

L16: ## 53.2 Curves and function fields
L17: 
L18: In this section we elaborate on the results of Varieties, Section 【11†33.4】 in the case of curves.
L19: 
L20: 【12†Lemma 53.2.1.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a curve and $Y$ a proper variety. Let $U \subset X$ be a nonempty open and let $f : U \to Y$ be a morphism. If $x \in X$ is a closed point such that $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a discrete valuation ring, then there exist an open $U \subset U' \subset X$ containing $x$ and a morphism of varieties $f' : U' \to Y$ extending $f$.
L21: Proof. This is a special case of Morphisms, Lemma 【13†29.43.5】. $\square$
L22: 
L23: 【14†Lemma 53.2.2.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a normal curve and $Y$ a proper variety. The set of rational maps from $X$ to $Y$ is the same as the set of morphisms $X \to Y$.
L24: Proof. A rational map from $X$ to $Y$ can be extended to a morphism $X \to Y$ by Lemma 【12†53.2.1】 as every local ring is a discrete valuation ring (for example by Varieties, Lemma 【15†33.43.8】). Conversely, if two morphisms $f,g: X \to Y$ are equivalent as rational maps, then $f = g$ by Morphisms, Lemma 【16†29.7.10】. $\square$
L25: 
L26: 【17†Lemma 53.2.3.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a nonconstant morphism of curves over $k$. If $Y$ is normal, then $f$ is flat.
L27: Proof. Pick $x \in X$ mapping to $y \in Y$. Then $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$ is either a field or a discrete valuation ring (Varieties, Lemma 【15†33.43.8】). Since $f$ is nonconstant it is dominant (as it must map the generic point of $X$ to the generic point of $Y$). This implies that $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is injective (Morphisms, Lemma 【18†29.8.8】).
L28: Hence $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is torsion free as a $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$-module and therefore $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat as a $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$-module by More on Algebra, Lemma 【19†15.22.10】. $\square$
L29: 【20†Lemma 53.2.4.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $k$. Assume
L30: 
L31:   1. $Y$ is separated over $k$,
L32: 
L33:   2. $X$ is proper of dimension $\leq 1$ over $k$,
L34: 
L35:   3. $f(Z)$ has at least two points for every irreducible component $Z \subset X$ of dimension $1$.
L36: 
L37: Then $f$ is finite.
L38: Proof. The morphism $f$ is proper by Morphisms, Lemma 【21†29.42.7】. Thus $f(X)$ is closed and images of closed points are closed. Let $y \in Y$ be the image of a closed point in $X$. Then $f^{-1}(\{ y\} )$ is a closed subset of $X$ not containing any of the generic points of irreducible components of dimension $1$ by condition (3). It follows that $f^{-1}(\{ y\} )$ is finite.
L39: Hence $f$ is finite over an open neighbourhood of $y$ by More on Morphisms, Lemma 【22†37.44.2】 (if $Y$ is Noetherian, then you can use the easier Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 【23†30.21.2】). Since we've seen above that there are enough of these points $y$, the proof is complete. $\square$
L40: 【24†Lemma 53.2.5.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of varieties with $Y$ proper and $X$ a curve. There exists a factorization $X \to \overline{X} \to Y$ where $X \to \overline{X}$ is an open immersion and $\overline{X}$ is a projective curve.
L41: 
L42: Proof. This is clear from Lemma 【12†53.2.1】 and Varieties, Lemma 【25†33.43.6】. $\square$
L43: Here is the main theorem of this section. We will say a morphism $f : X \to Y$ of varieties is constant if the image $f(X)$ consists of a single point $y$ of $Y$. If this happens then $y$ is a closed point of $Y$ (since the image of a closed point of $X$ will be a closed point of $Y$).
L44: 
L45: 【26†Theorem 53.2.6.】 Let $k$ be a field. The following categories are canonically equivalent
L46: 
L47:   1. The category of finitely generated field extensions $K/k$ of transcendence degree $1$.
L48:   2. The category of curves and dominant rational maps.
L49: 
L50:   3. The category of normal projective curves and nonconstant morphisms.
L51: 
L52:   4. The category of nonsingular projective curves and nonconstant morphisms.
L53: 
L54:   5. The category of regular projective curves and nonconstant morphisms.
L55: 
L56:   6. The category of normal proper curves and nonconstant morphisms.
L57: Proof. The equivalence between categories (1) and (2) is the restriction of the equivalence of Varieties, Theorem 【27†33.4.1】. Namely, a variety is a curve if and only if its function field has transcendence degree $1$, see for example Varieties, Lemma 【28†33.20.3】.
L58: The categories in (3), (4), (5), and (6) are the same. First of all, the terms “regular” and “nonsingular” are synonyms, see Properties, Definition 【29†28.9.1】. Being normal and regular are the same thing for Noetherian $1$-dimensional schemes (Properties, Lemmas 【30†28.9.4】 and 【31†28.12.6】). See Varieties, Lemma 【15†33.43.8】 for the case of curves. Thus (3) is the same as (5). Finally, (6) is the same as (3) by Varieties, Lemma 【32†33.43.4】.
L59: If $f : X \to Y$ is a nonconstant morphism of nonsingular projective curves, then $f$ sends the generic point $\eta $ of $X$ to the generic point $\xi $ of $Y$. Hence we obtain a morphism $k(Y) = \mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi } \to \mathcal{O}_{X, \eta } = k(X)$ in the category (1). If two morphisms $f,g: X \to Y$ gives the same morphism $k(Y) \to k(X)$, then by the equivalence between (1) and (2), $f$ and $g$ are equivalent as rational maps, so $f=g$ by Lemma 【14†53.2.2】.
L60: Conversely, suppose that we have a map $k(Y) \to k(X)$ in the category (1). Then we obtain a morphism $U \to Y$ for some nonempty open $U \subset X$. By Lemma 【12†53.2.1】 this extends to all of $X$ and we obtain a morphism in the category (5). Thus we see that there is a fully faithful functor (5)$\to $(1).
L61: To finish the proof we have to show that every $K/k$ in (1) is the function field of a normal projective curve. We already know that $K = k(X)$ for some curve $X$. After replacing $X$ by its normalization (which is a variety birational to $X$) we may assume $X$ is normal (Varieties, Lemma 【33†33.27.1】). Then we choose $X \to \overline{X}$ with $\overline{X} \setminus X = \{ x_1, \ldots , x_ n\} $ as in Varieties, Lemma 【25†33.43.6】.
L62: Since $X$ is normal and since each of the local rings $\mathcal{O}_{\overline{X}, x_ i}$ is normal we conclude that $\overline{X}$ is a normal projective curve as desired. (Remark: We can also first compactify using Varieties, Lemma 【34†33.43.5】 and then normalize using Varieties, Lemma 【33†33.27.1】. Doing it this way we avoid using the somewhat tricky Morphisms, Lemma 【35†29.54.16】.) $\square$
L63: 【36†Definition 53.2.7.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a curve. A nonsingular projective model of $X$ is a pair $(Y, \varphi )$ where $Y$ is a nonsingular projective curve and $\varphi : k(X) \to k(Y)$ is an isomorphism of function fields.
L64: A nonsingular projective model is determined up to unique isomorphism by Theorem 【26†53.2.6】. Thus we often say “the nonsingular projective model”. We usually drop $\varphi $ from the notation. Warning: it needn't be the case that $Y$ is smooth over $k$ but Lemma 【37†53.2.8】 shows this can only happen in positive characteristic.
L65: 
L66: 【37†Lemma 53.2.8.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a curve and let $Y$ be the nonsingular projective model of $X$. If $k$ is perfect, then $Y$ is a smooth projective curve.
L67: Proof. See Varieties, Lemma 【15†33.43.8】 for example. $\square$
L68: 
L69: 【38†Lemma 53.2.9.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a geometrically irreducible curve over $k$. For a field extension $K/k$ denote $Y_ K$ a nonsingular projective model of $(X_ K)_{red}$.
L70: 
L71:   1. If $X$ is proper, then $Y_ K$ is the normalization of $X_ K$.
L72: 
L73:   2. There exists $K/k$ finite purely inseparable such that $Y_ K$ is smooth.
L74: 
L75:   3. Whenever $Y_ K$ is smooth【39†^{1}】 we have $H^0(Y_ K, \mathcal{O}_{Y_ K}) = K$.
L76:   4. Given a commutative diagram
L77: 
L78: \[ \xymatrix{ \Omega & K' \ar[l] \\ K \ar[u] & k \ar[l] \ar[u] } \]
L79: 
L80: of fields such that $Y_ K$ and $Y_{K'}$ are smooth, then $Y_\Omega = (Y_ K)_\Omega = (Y_{K'})_\Omega $.
L81: 
L82: Proof. Let $X'$ be a nonsingular projective model of $X$. Then $X'$ and $X$ have isomorphic nonempty open subschemes. In particular $X'$ is geometrically irreducible as $X$ is (some details omitted). Thus we may assume that $X$ is projective.
L83: Assume $X$ is proper. Then $X_ K$ is proper and hence the normalization $(X_ K)^\nu $ is proper as a scheme finite over a proper scheme (Varieties, Lemma 【33†33.27.1】 and Morphisms, Lemmas 【40†29.45.11】 and 【41†29.42.4】). On the other hand, $X_ K$ is irreducible as $X$ is geometrically irreducible. Hence $X_ K^\nu $ is proper, normal, irreducible, and birational to $(X_ K)_{red}$. This proves (1) because a proper curve is projective (Varieties, Lemma 【32†33.43.4】).

L23: 【8†Lemma 33.43.8.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a curve over $k$. Let $x \in X$ be a closed point. We think of $x$ as a (reduced) closed subscheme of $X$ with sheaf of ideals $\mathcal{I}$. The following are equivalent
L24: 
L25:   1. $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is regular,
L26: 
L27:   2. $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is normal,
L28: 
L29:   3. $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a discrete valuation ring,
L30: 
L31:   4. $\mathcal{I}$ is an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module,
L32: 
L33:   5. $x$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$.
L34: If $k$ is perfect or if $\kappa (x)$ is separable over $k$, these are also equivalent to
L35: 
L36:   1. $X \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(k)$ is smooth at $x$.
L37: Proof. Since $X$ is a curve, the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension $1$ (Lemma 【15†33.20.3】). Parts (4) and (5) are equivalent by definition and are equivalent to $\mathcal{I}_ x = \mathfrak m_ x \subset \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ having one generator (Divisors, Lemma 【16†31.16.2】). The equivalence of (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5) therefore follows from Algebra, Lemma 【17†10.119.7】. The final statement follows from Lemma 【18†33.25.8】 in case $k$ is perfect.
L38: If $\kappa (x)/k$ is separable, then the equivalence follows from Algebra, Lemma 【19†10.140.5】. $\square$
